u_ground.text: The ground moves through it at about a thousand and forty miles an hour.

u_gust.text: The strongest gust ever measured was about two hundred and fifty miles an hour.

u_sea.text: At a twelve hour day the sea wants to stand about twenty miles higher at the equator.

u_depth.text: The ocean is only about two point three miles deep.

u_eq6.text: The equator moves at about forty-one hundred and fifty miles an hour.

u_speed3.text: The ground moves at about eighty-three hundred miles an hour.

u_w3.text: You weigh twenty-two percent less: a hundred and fifty pounds feels like a hundred and seventeen.

u_jump2.text: The jump that lifts you a foot and a half now lifts you about three feet.

u_w15.text: At an hour and a half you are almost weightless, about one eighth of your weight: a hundred and fifty pounds becomes about eighteen.

u_jump15.text: A foot-and-a-half jump carries you about thirteen feet, higher than a basketball hoop, and a cup falling off a table takes about three times as long to land.

u_l03.text: Right now the ground carries you at about a thousand and forty miles an hour.

u_l05.text: The ground moves at about two thousand and eighty miles an hour, nearly three times the speed of sound.

u_l15.text: At a day of an hour and twenty-four minutes, the ground moves at about seventeen thousand seven hundred miles an hour, the speed of a satellite in low orbit.

u_l18.text: So the next time you stand still, remember you're already moving at a thousand miles an hour.
